anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located at the optimizer's plan-selection stage, where the chosen execution plan is substantially sub-optimal due to the cost model, plan reuse, or context-dependent decisions even though the statistical inputs are reasonably accurate. It is distinct from statistics anomalies because the costing inputs are acceptable but the decision logic produces a poor plan. Observable phenomena: identical statement text producing very different plans across executions, sudden switches from selective index access to full scans, nested-loop blowouts driven by high outer-side cardinality, unexpected gain or loss of parallelism, plan changes immediately following a configuration change, version upgrade, or plan-cache invalidation, and large gaps between the cached plan cost and the actual execution cost. Possible contributing factors: bind-value-sensitive plan reuse with skewed parameter values, plan-cache pollution and excessive ad-hoc plans, optimizer version or default cost-model changes after upgrades, lack of plan-stability mechanisms such as plan baselines, stored hints, or query-fingerprint plan stores, partition-pruning failures, and cost-model parameters not aligned with the actual hardware characteristics.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
